title: Jazzy Japanese Pork Tan Tan Udon
description: A citrusy and creamy Japanese dish featuring minced pork and binchotan-charcoal, with anti-inflammatory friendly ingredients, served as a tan-tan-udon.
instructions: Start by smoking the binchotan charcoal until it is covered in a thin layer of ash.
In a large pan, heat the sesame oil over medium heat and add the grated ginger and minced garlic.
Cook the ginger and garlic for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the minced pork to the pan, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until it is no longer pink.
Add the turmeric, soy sauce, and yuzu juice to the pan, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and let cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the pork mixture is cooking, cook the udon noodles according to the package instructions.
To serve, place the cooked noodles in a bowl, top with the pork mixture, and garnish with thinly sliced green onions.
Use the smoked binchotan charcoal to add a smoky flavor to the dish, if desired.
